subject: Cloud Computing
title: Serverless Architecture
description: A micro-lesson that makes Serverless Architecture usable.

hook.text: No servers to manage. No capacity to plan. Write a function, deploy it, and the cloud runs it when needed.

buildup.text: Serverless platforms like AWS Lambda and Azure Functions execute code in response to events — then shut down.

discovery.text: You pay per execution, not per hour. Zero traffic means zero cost. It's the purest pay-as-you-go model.

twist.text: Cold starts — the delay when a function hasn't run recently — add seconds of latency. That matters for real-time apps.

climax.text: Serverless is ideal for event-driven, bursty workloads. For always-on services, containers are usually better.

punchline.text: No servers to manage. Just code that runs when needed.

quiz.question: What is a cold start in serverless computing?
options: A delay when a function that hasn't run recently needs to initialize before executing
When a serverless function crashes due to low temperatures in the data center
The time it takes to write and deploy a new serverless function

details.summary: Serverless architecture lets developers write functions that run on demand without managing servers. The cloud provider handles provisioning, scaling, and patching. You pay only for actual execution time, often measured in milliseconds.
details.whyItMatters: Serverless eliminates infrastructure management for event-driven workloads. It can drastically reduce costs for sporadic traffic and accelerate development by removing operational overhead.
takeaways: No servers to provision, patch, or manage
Billing is based on actual execution time
Scales automatically from zero to thousands of instances

faq.question: What are the limitations of serverless?
faq.answer: Cold starts add latency when functions have not been invoked recently. Execution time limits typically cap at 15 minutes. Debugging distributed serverless systems is harder. Vendor lock-in is significant because function runtimes differ between providers.

faq.question: When is serverless the wrong choice?
faq.answer: Long-running processes, workloads with predictable high throughput, and applications needing specialized hardware like GPUs are poor fits. Consistent high-volume traffic may also be cheaper on reserved instances than pay-per-invocation serverless.
